subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Hydraulic Cylinders: Linear Force
description: A fast breakdown of Hydraulic Cylinders: Linear Force for builders.

hook.text: A hydraulic cylinder converts fluid pressure into a straight push or pull. It's the muscle of heavy machinery.

buildup.text: Oil enters one side of the piston and pushes it outward. The rod extends, applying force to the load.

discovery.text: Force equals pressure times piston area. A 10-centimeter piston at 200 bar pushes with over 15 tons of force.

twist.text: The rod side has less area than the cap side. Retraction is faster but weaker. Extension is slower but stronger.

climax.text: Excavator arms, dump truck beds, and aircraft landing gear all depend on hydraulic cylinders for controlled motion.

punchline.text: Oil in, rod out. That's how machines lift the world.

quiz.question: Why is a hydraulic cylinder stronger during extension than retraction?
options: The pump delivers more pressure during the extension stroke
The cap side has a larger piston area than the rod side, creating more force
The oil flows faster during extension, building more momentum
